CI health: facebookexperimental/triton

MI350 · B200 · H100 GPU workflows · data as of … · refreshed every 3 h

Latest status

green is better

PR, 24 h = every PR run started in the last 24 h; a red PR run is often the PR’s own fault, so this is a summary, not the latest run. Green only when every finished run passed; the test / infra split is detail, explained in the trend views below. The purpose table counts every run where that test step finished, including runs later cancelled, so it can show a failure the run-level count does not. – = not run for that trigger (TLX perf runs only on nightlies). Push = the newest run triggered by a land on main (PR-scope test selection does not apply; it runs the full job set its paths filter allows). Nightly = the newest scheduled run, every 6 h. Ages count from when the run started. Only nightly ages turn red (after 7 h): pushes depend on what lands and on path filters, so long gaps are normal. Groups come from step names via groups.yml: TLX core = Run TLX core tests, Tutorial correctness = Run TLX tutorial correctness tests, TLX codegen = Run device-agnostic TLX codegen tests, TritonBench = *-tritonbench-test (formerly *-meta-triton-test), Gluon = Run Gluon tests (python/test/gluon), Runtime = Run runtime unit tests, TLX perf = Run host-default TLX L2 perf.

Usage

Runner minutes per successful PR run, by job

↓ lower is better

Average job time per successful PR run, by ISO week (Monday start), over every successful PR run that week. Build runs on a CPU runner; the rest on GPU runners. Reporting jobs are left out.

GPU hours per day, by run outcome

↓ lower is better; failed + cancelled hours are waste

Sum of job start-to-finish times on GPU runners (labels without ubuntu), split by how the run ended. The wheel build runs on a CPU runner and is left out.

Status

Pass rate by workflow and trigger

↑ higher is better

One line per trigger, never blended: a red nightly and a red PR mean different things. Pass rate = passed ÷ (passed + failed); cancelled runs are left out. Dashed lines mark commits on main that changed the GPU workflow files.

Why runs failed, per day

↓ fewer is better; infra and perf should reach 0

Failed runs by cause, all triggers combined. Classified from the failed step names: infra = setup, wheel download or install, credentials, runner lost; config = startup_failure; perf = only perf steps failed; test = any test step failed.

Every nightly on main, last 14 days

more ✓ is better

Each column is one scheduled run (every 6 h); each row a test group, mapped from step names. A grey rule marks the first nightly after a commit that changed the GPU workflow files.

Rebuilt every 3 h from GitHub Actions data by .github/scripts/ci_health.py; the rules are in ci_health_rules.py. Raw data: the ci-health release. Computed data: data.json.
